correctness.rationale: The continuous optimum is reconstructed from Fejer-Riesz factorization and the top eigenvalue of a path adjacency matrix. The explicit extremizer has a completely identified contact set. Positive contact weights give the sharp upper bound on meshes divisible by 2(n+2). For a hypothetical off-mesh equality, finite LP duality forces every dual optimizer onto the continuous contact set; Chebyshev-Vandermonde uniqueness forces positive mass at every distinct contact cosine, and the contact fractions 3/(2(n+2)) and 5/(2(n+2)) then force the full divisibility. Unbounded aliased cases are handled separately. The included checker corroborates the algebraic identities and exact contact-grid arithmetic but is not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The discretized Carathéodory-Fejér problem is a canonical finite relaxation of a classical extremal problem. The result gives a complete arithmetic classification of all grids with zero relaxation gap in every degree n >= 3, rather than a numerical table or isolated small case. The contact-set rigidity and exact divisibility mechanism are reusable structural information for finite positive-definite and sampling problems.
